paths.title: The cheapest insurer does not automatically win.
paths.description: Choose what matters most to you. The result keeps all three answers separate, so the difference is immediately clear.

items.title: Save on contributions
items.heading: How much could you save on contributions?
items.description: Income, insurance status and region all matter. We show the lowest suitable price anchor and useful alternatives behind it.
checks: Classify monthly gross income and insurance status
Compare only insurers available in your region
Show other low-cost options next to the price leader
items.resultTitle: A clear euro difference instead of percentage clutter
items.resultBody: You see what the difference means per month and per year. Reputation and service can then be part of a conscious decision.

items.title: Use a bonus
items.heading: Which bonus can you realistically achieve?
items.description: An advertised maximum is not useful on its own. What matters is which activities you already do or can reliably complete.
checks: Select preventive care, vaccinations and activity realistically
Keep cash bonuses and earmarked credits separate
Explain deadlines, evidence and programme duration
items.resultTitle: Your achievable bonus, not an advertising maximum
items.resultBody: We only calculate with information that fits you. The actual bonus always depends on the insurer, its conditions and verified activities.

items.title: Find better benefits
items.heading: Which insurer offers more for your routine?
items.description: Sometimes a specific benefit matters more than the final euro of savings, for example for families, osteopathy, dental cleaning or digital service.
checks: Make the particular strengths of insurers visible
Do not combine cost, bonus and benefits into a fictional total
items.resultTitle: A benefit match you can understand
items.resultBody: You can see why an insurer fits your needs and which alternative may be cheaper or stronger on benefits.

everyday.title: You do not need to be a competitive athlete.
everyday.description: Many bonus programmes also recognise ordinary health routines. You only select what genuinely applies to you.
items: Check-ups for children and during pregnancy
everyday.note: Each insurer sets its own rules for eligible activities, evidence and whether it pays cash or an earmarked reimbursement.

transparency.title: The result should be real.
transparency.description: That is why we distinguish between a reliable contribution difference, an expected achievable bonus and particular benefits.

items.title: A bonus is not guaranteed
items.text: It depends on programme rules and the activities you actually complete and verify.

items.title: Cash is not the same as credit
items.text: Freely available cash and earmarked reimbursements are shown separately.

items.title: Regional really means regional
items.text: An insurer is only compared if it is available where you live or work.

items.q: Do I need to switch before seeing the comparison?
items.a: No. You see your result first and then decide whether you want to start an application.

items.q: Is the cheapest insurer always recommended?
items.a: No. The cheapest suitable insurer is a clear price anchor. We also show alternatives when bonus, benefits, reputation or service matter more to you.
No. Bonus payments depend on the insurer's rules and the activities you actually complete and document. A responsible result distinguishes between a possible and a realistically achievable bonus.

items.q: Can a health insurance bonus pay for supplementary cover?
items.a: Depending on the achievable bonus and premium, this may be possible in part or in full. It is not guaranteed. Cash bonuses and earmarked reimbursements must be considered separately.

items.q: Does the comparison work for families?
items.a: Yes. Income, insurance status, children and personal circumstances belong in the calculation because they can affect contributions, long-term care insurance and eligible bonus activities.
